I'm not sure if this is such a good example of censorship. After all, it was genuinely a repost.
i thought it was not possible to repost the same article to the same sub.

They both link to the same article. However, the URLs differ slightly:

Original:

http://www.washingtonpost.com/news/the-intersect/wp/2015/02/18/the-reddit-exodus-is-a-perfect-illustration-of-the-state-of-free-speech-on-the-web/

Repost:

http://www.washingtonpost.com/news/the-intersect/wp/2015/02/18/the-reddit-exodus-is-a-perfect-illustration-of-the-state-of-free-speech-on-the-web/?lol

The reposter seems to have added "?lol" to the end of the URL, which won't change which page it links to, but will circumvent the sub's repost prevention.
So technically this is not a repost

It's the same thing, so it's a repost. The only difference is that the second poster abused the Washington Post's 404 redirect. It's not that great of an article anyway. It's just the "journalist" talking about how terrible Reddit is and how Voat will be even worse. The writer didn't even go to voat to look into what they were writing about, they just assumed it would be terrible.

Well, they didn't abuse the 404 redirect per say. URLs are built up of multiple sections: the protocol (http://), the domain name (www.washingtonpost.com), the path (/news/the-intersect/etc), and the parameters (?lol, anything after the question mark). (Technically, there's also the anchor (anything after a #), but that isn't relevant here.) The web server looks at that URL and just finds the article specified by the path. The parameters aren't part of the path, so it just ignores that and carries on with its busy web server life. Nothing is redirected, nothing 404s, the ?lol is simply ignored because it's not part of the relevant section of the URL.

Other than that though, I agree.
Well I learned my thing for the day.

I just asked the mod where their rule is about reposts being deleted (I'll edit if i get a reply). I don't see any rules like that in their sidebar. I know what you're saying about reposts, but that's (IMO) what the voting system is for. Let the redditors decide what they want to see (or discuss) again; don't decide it for them. This post had the same amount of upvotes as the one posted two days prior, and roughly the same % up/down. That indicates that there is still interest in the story, and some people may have missed the link two days before. The forum was a potential opportunity for more discussion to take place.

In addition, r/technology states that reddiquette applies in the sub. From its "Please Don't" section:

Complain about other users reposting/rehosting stories, images, videos, or any other content. Users should give credit where credit should be given, but if someone fails to do so, and is not causing harm, please either don't point it out, or point it out politely and leave it at that. They are only earning karma, which has little to no use at all.

Complain about reposts. Just because you have seen it before doesn't mean everyone has. Votes indicate the popularity of a post, so just vote. Keep in mind that linking to previous posts is not automatically a complaint; it is information.

Basically the mod has decided on behalf of the whole community that they are all sick of seeing this link and having this discussion, and he's nice enough to quietly remove the post before it ever hits their screens. And all the other people who wanted to discuss this topic with fellow redditors, or people who aren't on the site every day and may have missed the post the first time -- well I guess they won't know about voat now like us, right?

I'm not sure I agree with their decision to crackdown on the repost either, I'm still not convinced it's an example of censorship. At least as far as I can see, their rules seem to be rather vague, leaving a lot up to interpretation, which would mean that the individual moderator's personal opinion on reposts comes in to play.

As far as I know, the reddiquette is mostly targeted at users; saying users shouldn't bitch about reposts isn't the same as saying that mods shouldn't delete them.

Also, one moderator's reply on what the rules are regarding reposts may not necessarily be all that relevant. As I mentioned eralier, the subreddit's rules are rather vague. I'm a founder of, and still affiliated with, an online community with similarly vague guidelines which leave a lot up to the individual staff member's interpretation, and while that has worked rather well so far, it does mean that depending on which staff member you ask, their interpretation of the rules and their practice may differ.

Of course, none of this is proof that what this moderator is doing isn't censorship. I'm just trying to maintain a healthy skepticism, and whether or not this should be interpreted as an act of censorship depends on the subreddit's history of censorship and how they historically have handled reposts to the same article approximately one day apart, neither of which I know enough about to really take a stance.

EDIT: Also, make sure to keep us updated if you ever receive a reply from that moderator. It would be interesting to hear, and things would for sure be suspicious if the reply was something along the lines of them having a rather strict policy to not ban reposts.

I haven't heard anything back yet, but I'll let you know. I doubt, after considering it, that the answer will be anything other than "We have a way of preventing the same link from being posted twice to the same sub. This user found a way to circumvent our automated method, so this was just a manual application of that mechanism."

Maybe I should have clarified that I shared the same opinion as you, but I got off on a bit of a tangent. I wouldn't call it censorship in its conventionally used sense. I thought that it may, however, indicate how nonchalantly a mod can delete a story before the community has a chance to tell the mod what they think of it. Upon further thought, and realizing that this was the exact same link, I don't think the mod was technically in the wrong. Were this a different link from another source covering the same story and it was deleted, there may be cause to question why the post was deleted. But I think more stories may be coming soon anyway, so we can wait and see.

Thanks for giving some balance to my reply, too. I agree that it's good to keep healthy skepticism, and I appreciate you providing more information and helping to keep my own skepticism in check.
